utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like document ID D67 and 67A to be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: They will be Exhibits D67 and D67A. I must correct the previous exhibit numbers. They should be D66/1 and D66/1A. I've read through the transcript, the passages shown to me by the court deputy in relation to that previous one that was in dispute, 85. It was not admitted into evidence then, but it now has been.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would just like to ask you for another correction, in view of 67. It also has 67/1. So it's 67 and 67/1, and both documents have respective translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately, that didn't come out in the transcript, and I don't think I heard it either. But anyway, we'll add to that. There should be Exhibits 67/1 and 67/1A.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I beg your pardon, there is quite a confusion with these numbers. My colleague, Mr. Vasic, tells me that in the transcript "66/2" is missing, because there is 66, 66/1, and 66/2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bakrac, we can only go on the transcript and the interpretation. I see no reference anywhere to "/2." But that was tendered, was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, my mistake, because I did not see the third page when I was tendering it. It is my mistake only, and my colleague Mr. Vasic just signalled that to me now, that there is a document with "/2" as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Kuo, any objection to "/1" and "/2"?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well, then. We shall add yet again 66/2 and 66/2A.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, and I do apologise once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, financing that part of the KP Dom and the economic unit that you headed, was that one of the duties of the Ministry of Justice?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the KP Dom was established by the Ministry of Justice and it was their duty to finance the workers and employees who belonged to the Drina Economic Unit of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: For the work of the KP Dom, was there a certain budget that was envisaged and budgetary resources?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC
utterances.text: I was told that that's the way it was done before as well, before the war conflict broke out; that there was always supposed to be a budget and that was the case during the war operations as well. There was supposed to be a budget.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you get anything from the ministry?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC
utterances.text: Very little. Almost nothing. A little bit was received, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to show the witness ID D84, please, and perhaps for the sake of brevity, 83 as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please just take a look at this document and tell us whether this is your signature on this document and whether the stamp is that of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC
utterances.text: It is my signature, and it says here "Upravnik." Yes, yes, as long as it's my signature, it must be the stamp of the KP Dom as well. The stamp must be authentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to tender 84 and 84A into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What about 83? I thought you asked him to look at 83 as well. Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. But the usher did not have his headphones on so he only took document 84 and showed it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection to 84?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: They will be Exhibits D84 and D84A.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, would you please be so kind as to look at this. This is a letter to the Ministry of the Economy where a certain quantity of oil is being requested so that the KP Dom could function. Is this your signature on this document? And why did you address yourself to the Ministry of the Economy?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC
utterances.text: It is my signature, and due to the circumstances involved, and the difficulties in providing proper supplies of oil and oil derivatives and maintaining four-and-a-half-thousand hens, and then also there were swines and pigs. It was very difficult to get oil derivatives. So I had to ask them for that, let them know that I asked for it. If they give some, let them give it. I thought it was proper for them to see how agile I was and that I asked for it, and that's why I asked for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Krnojelac. The Defence would like document ID D83 and 83A, the translation, to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: They will be Exhibits D83 and 83A. There is hardly time for the usher to get over to you and get back again by 4.00. We will adjourn now until 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: 3.59 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday the 26th day of June, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.
